# Academic profile

Physician-epidemiologist and Chief Assistant Professor in the Department of Social Medicine and Public Health at the Medical University of Plovdiv, working at the intersection of epidemiology, health economics and health policy. Research centres on how health systems allocate scarce resources — orphan medicines and rare cancers, the cost of illness, health technology assessment, and the health consequences of the urban environment — using routinely collected administrative health data and real-world evidence.

Holds an MD, a PhD in social medicine and public health, an MPH, and master's degrees in economics and finance, statistical business consulting, and impact assessment and policy appraisal, and is currently reading for a Master of Laws. Board-certified in Social Medicine and Organisation of Health Care and Pharmacy, and currently in residency training in Infectious Disease Epidemiology.

Develops and publishes open research software: [`kkstatfun`](kkstatfun.qmd), an R toolkit of 146 functions for medical statistics, epidemiology and health economics. Associate Editor at JMIR Publications and founder of the Social Epidemiology Lab.

# Research interests

Epidemiology · Social medicine and public health · Infectious disease epidemiology · Health policy and health technology assessment · Real-world evidence and health economics · Environmental and urban health · Biostatistics and reproducible research

The publication record is organised around six research programmes:

1. **Rare diseases, rare cancers and access to orphan medicines.** Policy analysis of definitions, registration, organisation of care and reimbursement; timeliness of market access; national and EU-level policy alternatives.
2. **Health economics, HTA and real-world evidence.** Cost-of-illness studies (myasthenia gravis, spinal muscular atrophy, osteoporosis, end-stage kidney disease, terminal cancer), budget-impact validation, and public expenditure analysis from a payer perspective.
3. **Infectious disease epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance.** COVID-19 epidemiology and vaccine impact, urinary tract and sexually transmitted infections, antimicrobial resistance trends, echinococcosis, and HPV-attributable expenditure.
4. **Environmental and urban health.** Air pollution and cardiovascular risk, green space and land cover, health impact assessment in spatial planning, and stakeholder evidence for urban environmental policy.
5. **Health professions education and digital health.** Virtual-reality and simulation-based training, trauma-informed care, and mental health literacy among school and health professionals.
6. **Applied biostatistics, prediction and reproducible research.** External validation of clinical prediction and AI tools, diagnostic accuracy, and open, reproducible statistical software.

# Research software and open science

`2024 – Present`

- **[`kkstatfun`](kkstatfun.qmd)** — R package for medical statistics, epidemiology and health economics. A single tidy, pipe-friendly and `group_by()`-aware interface covering measures of association, standardisation, diagnostic accuracy, agreement, survival analysis, regression, causal inference and quasi-experimental designs, health technology assessment, and infectious disease modelling. Current release **v1.3.0**, 146 functions, MIT licence.
    - Source: [github.com/kostadinoff/kkstatfun](https://github.com/kostadinoff/kkstatfun) · Archive: [doi:10.5281/zenodo.18936019](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18936019) · Documentation: [kkstatfun function reference](kkstatfun.qmd)

`2025`

- **PhD dissertation appendices and analysis code** — reproducible materials accompanying the doctoral thesis on health policies in rare tumours: [github.com/kostadinoff/phd_appendices](https://github.com/kostadinoff/phd_appendices)

`Ongoing`

- **Reproducible analytical workflows** — Quarto-based reproducible reporting for manuscripts, teaching materials and policy analyses; version-controlled research workflows in Git and GitHub; literate analysis pipelines in R with figures and tables regenerated from source data.
- **Open educational and scholarly resources** — [kostadinoff.github.io](https://kostadinoff.github.io): teaching slides, 15-minute learning modules, learning tasks and the *Epi News* research digest, all published openly and generated from source (see *Teaching materials and textbooks*).

# Research methods expertise

- **Observational epidemiology** — cohort, case–control and cross-sectional designs; retrospective analysis of routinely collected administrative health data
- **Regression modelling** — linear, logistic, ordinal, Poisson and modified-Poisson models; model specification, validation and calibration
- **Survival analysis** — Kaplan–Meier estimation, Cox proportional hazards models, restricted mean survival time and competing risks
- **Longitudinal and time-series methods** — trend analysis, interrupted time series and surveillance analytics
- **Health-economic evaluation** — cost-of-illness, cost-effectiveness and budget-impact analysis; probabilistic sensitivity analysis
- **Real-world evidence** — analysis of payer, registry and hospital administrative datasets
- **Diagnostic accuracy and prediction** — sensitivity and specificity, ROC and AUC analysis, external validation, agreement and reliability
- **Evidence synthesis** — systematic, scoping and rapid reviews
- **Bayesian analysis** — Bayesian estimation with informative and sceptical priors
- **Reproducible statistical programming** — literate, version-controlled analysis pipelines and open research software
